I expected to see big discounts on older models of the Garmin Fenix this Black Friday, and you can save big on the Fenix 8 or Fenix 8 Pro right now, but I didn’t think Garmin would reduce the new Fenix 9.

I’m delighted to be wrong on this one, because the entire Garmin Fenix 9 line-up is currently $100 off, the first notable discount the watch has got since it launched in late August.

There are a lot of models to pick between in the sale, but the model I tested and use to track my own training is the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro, which is $1,099 at Amazon right now.

All models of the Garmin Fenix 9 are reduced by $100 for Black Friday, including the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro with InReach, which is the watch I tested for our review. It packs in all of Garmin's latest and greatest features, and looks great thanks to its all-titanium case.

The Garmin Fenix 9 line-up includes four models. The standard Fenix 9 and three variants of the Fenix 9 Pro, all of which offer a full titanium case as a key upgrade on the base Fenix 9.

When picking between Pro models you have to decide if you want an AMOLED or MIP display — you’ll find the latter on the Fenix 9 Pro Solar.

If you want the longest battery life possible on your Fenix, then opting for a Fenix 9 Pro Solar model is the smart move. The MIP display has solar panels on it to boost the battery life in sunny conditions, and the Pro Solar will outlast the AMOLED models of the Fenix 9.

You also have to make the call on whether you want a Pro model with InReach, giving you extra connectivity when you’re in the great outdoors.

Another major decision is the size you go for — there are 43mm, 47mm and 51mm options, with the battery life and screen size growing with the case size.

I tested the 51mm model, which lasts me over 10 days on a charge with the screen always-on, but it is a large watch and those with slim wrists might prefer a smaller size.

All of the Fenix 9 models offers great design and outstanding sports tracking and navigation features, and they also have useful smarts like music storage with the ability to link up with streaming services.

You can still save more by opting for an older Fenix, and the Garmin Fenix 8 Pro is $849 at Amazon right now, a great deal on a watch that has Garmin’s LTE and satellite connectivity.

The Garmin Fenix 8 Pro still offers better value than the Fenix 9 in the sales thanks to this $350 saving. While the Fenix 9 Pro has a few handy updates and a more attractive all-titanium design, the older watch matches it on key features and is much cheaper.

However, if you want to get the latest model, you can now do so for $100 less, and given how new the Fenix 9 is I think any saving at all is a surprise bonus this Black Friday.

#3272. The Best Last-Minute Gifts That Don't Feel Last Minute

This series will help you pick the perfect presents, decor, and activities to make this Christmas the Best Christmas Ever.

We’ve all experienced gift panic—that sinking feeling when you realize you need a present in an hour and you just don’t have one to give. Whether you spent all year chasing the “perfect” gift or simply procrastinated, your time is nearly up. But don’t panic. The clock may have nearly run out, but your options haven’t. Before you resort to re-gifting something from the back of a closet, here’s how to pull off a last-minute gift that is effortless but feels elevated and worthy of the person you’re giving it to.

With the right presentation, even the most last-minute gift can read as thoughtful. Any performer will tell you that the difference between a good show and a bad one comes down to commitment and confidence. The same is true for last-minute gifts: If you act like your gift is thoughtful and intentional, they’ll think it is. The biggest mistake people make is apologizing as they hand over a present—nothing ruins a vibe faster than, “Sorry this is so last-minute.” So give with confidence.

And focus on presentation. A handwritten note that contains a shared memory or personal joke can elevate a present. Use simple but personal wrapping; craft paper and twine, or a reusable gift bag that looks like you planned ahead. Add a small flourish, like a sprig of holly or a fancy bow. Small touches can make it seem like you’ve carefully prepared. What you don’t want are obvious panic gifts that scream, “I grabbed this on the way here.” The goal is effortless, not frantic.

Digital gifts are your friends. You can order something in minutes that arrives instantly online, and with a little thought, will still read as personal and intentional. The trick is choosing a present that speaks to the recipient’s tastes, hobbies, or quirks, and pairing it with a small note to show you remember what they love. From e-books to streaming subscriptions, these gifts hit the sweet spot of thoughtful and last-minute. Here are some suggestion:

When time is running out, gift cards are your secret weapon. They arrive instantly online, don’t require shipping, and with the right presentation, they can feel surprisingly thoughtful. The key is to pick a card that fits the recipient’s interests and add a personal note. The more specific you are, the better. If your giftee is into Italian food, get them an Eataly gift card. If they're a PC gamer, get them a Steam card. If they're into education, a membership to Skillshare is perfect. There's a gift card out there for just about any interest, and all you have to do it google it and email it.

Generic gift cards can be a last-minute lifesaver that can still seem a little personal if you give them the right way.

Pick a theme or design: Many online cards, like Amazon, Etsy, or Starbucks, let you choose designs. The right visual makes the card feel more intentional.

Include a warm, personal message: Even one line can make a digital card feel thoughtful—something like, “I couldn’t pick just one thing for you. Hope this helps you treat yourself.”

Send strategically: Deliver the card by email or text, but consider printing the email or screenshotting it in a small envelope so it feels like a “real” gift.

Sign someone up for a subscription service, write a note explaining you want to keep giving them presents all year, and you're golden. Here are some suggestions:

SnackCrate: This service sends a different snack from around the world every month.

SpiceClub: For the culinary adventurer on your list. A subscription to RawSpiceBar’s Spice Club delivers a curated selection of spices every month.

Mocktail Club: Booze-free fancy drinks delivered once a month? Sign me up.

Thera Box: If you know someone in need of some self-care, this once-a-month box is packed with wellness and relaxation items.

Loot Crate: If your giftee is geeky, consider this monthly surprise box of pop culture treasures.

Cameo is a platform where celebrities, influencers, musicians, and performers create personalized video messages for fans. If someone on your list is a fan of someone on Cameo, you can set up a session, and give a card with a mysterious note like "Keep an eye out for a special message." They'll be delighted with a personal message from wrestling legend Mick Foley or terrified when Chris Hansen appears on their screen; your choice.

I have enough crap in my house, so I love getting experiences instead of things. The challenge with experience gifts is usually timing: Many require reservations or coordination, but there are plenty of options that let your giftee schedule the time, making them perfect last-minute gifts.

Museum membership cards: Many institutions sell digital gift memberships that the recipient can activate whenever they like.

Movie tickets: Your local multiplex probably has a gift certificate you can buy online.

Local attraction passes: Some city attractions offer gift cards or “anytime admission” tickets that don’t expire immediately.

Pair these with a note explaining why you chose the experience, or, if you have that kind of relationship, something like, "I want to take you to the Museum of Modern Art." Just make sure you follow through and actually go.

Sometimes, there’s literally no time to order, wrap, or even think about a gift. If you’re scrambling out the door and need something now, you might be able to fake your way through, even if you're stopping at the liquor store on the way to the Christmas party.

Flowers or a small potted plant: Give a seasonal bouquet or a small indoor plant. Add a handwritten note, even a single line, and it might come off as thoughtful.

Gourmet chocolates or candy: Specialty chocolates from a local shop or grocery store display can feel luxe with a little ribbon or bag.

Wine, craft beer, or non-alcoholic beverage: A bottle with a clean label or interesting packaging immediately elevates your gift. Ask the clerk at the liquor store to help you find something unique.

Lottery tickets: Who wouldn't appreciate a bunch of scratch-off lottery tickets?

Hard cash is the most impersonal gift of all, but the only one you know will be used. This gift really depends on the person getting it, so be aware of whether they're likely to think "Just what I wanted!" or "Wait, I'm not poor." If you give cash, make sure it's crisp bills in a nice card, with a personalized note.

iOS 27 includes a really clever new feature that aims to solve the awkward middle ground between cellular and Wi-Fi connectivity. Here’s how it works and how you can turn it on.

In a support document, Apple explains that Connectivity Assist uses cellular data to improve your connection when Wi-Fi is slow or unusable. Apple uses examples like your backyard or driveway, as well as “coffee shops, airports, sports venues, and everywhere in between.”

Essentially, the feature detects when your Wi-Fi connection is weak or unusable and intelligently uses cellular data to keep you connected.

One practical example I’ve noticed is when I walk out of my house and get in my car. Oftentimes, my iPhone will cling to my house’s weak Wi-Fi connection, making it hard to start playing Apple Music and queue up directions in Apple Maps.

Connectivity Assist solves that problem. My phone can now intelligently use cellular data to help that transition away from Wi-Fi. It’s one of many really nice quality-of-life improvements in iOS 27.

You can turn Connectivity Assist on or off with these steps:

Another thing to be aware of is that you might use more cellular data with Connectivity Assist turned on. You can monitor your data usage via your carrier’s app or website, as well as in the Settings app on iPhone.

#3268. Five recent tech outages were not due to AI; the next round will be

Five major tech outages in quick succession earlier this month led to speculation that they were connected, with some inevitably believing them to be AI-related.

That wasn’t the case, but the US Director of National Intelligence is one of a number of experts warning that we should expect AI-powered outages in the near future …

Earlier this month saw five tech outages, one after the other. A widespread Microsoft 365 outage occurred when two unrelated issues coincided. The next day saw a nationwide ground stop of US air traffic due to a communication issue affecting all air traffic control centers. A few days later, a bug in a Chase bank system saw disruption not only to the bank itself, but also other banks where Chase was a party to a transaction. Many Apple services went offline later the same week, with retail stores also affected. Finally, United Airlines had its own widespread IT outage that grounded a significant number of flights.

Each had their own unrelated causes, with the White House stating that rumors of an AI-facilitated systemic attack by a hostile state were false.

However, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton has warned that we should expect future tech outages as a result of attacks facilitated by AI-discovered vulnerabilities. CNBC reports him issuing the warning on CNN’s State of the Union.

The American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading our systems; they should be prepared for investment in cybersecurity, and they should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road.

You prepare by knowing that systems are going to be upgraded; they may be interrupted for a period of time and that companies and government are dealing with this on the front foot.

We already saw an example of this last month when a vulnerability discovered in PHP saw a significant number of websites being taken offline.

Microsoft President Brad Smith says it isn’t just a question of bad actors exploiting vulnerabilities discovered by AI, but companies rushing to patch these may inadvertently cause systems to fail, as Newsweek reports.

What AI did earlier this year was basically make it much easier for people to find vulnerabilities in code, and then you can either use that knowledge to patch the code, or if you’re a bad actor, you can use that knowledge to try to hack into systems.

Especially when you have older infrastructure, especially when you’re trying to patch at such a pace, especially when you have to go so fast that you can’t take as much time to test what you’re changing in the code, you do increase the risk of something going wrong.

Major IT failures look set to be a routine event in the coming weeks and months.

#3263. As Apple works on AI agent features, banks are already blocking them

One of the most dramatic shifts in the AI landscape is the emergence of intelligent agents that can use iPhone and Mac apps in order to carry out tasks on our behalf.

We can already use third-party chatbots in this way, and we know Apple is working hard to turn Siri AI into an agent. However, before the company even gets the chance, banks are already blocking them, and this may be just the start …

The science fiction promise of AI has always been to be able to tell a computer what we want done and have the task carried out for us automatically. That’s starting to turn into a reality with the emergence of AI agents.

We’ve already seen Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, and Muse gain agent capabilities, and Apple is expected to bring these to Siri AI at some point next year.

Earlier this month, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said that the company ultimately wants to go in this direction and may add these abilities next year. CEO John Ternus has reportedly been pushing Craig Federighi for faster software development, with specific mention of “moving beyond necessary improvements to Siri,” which seems likely to mean agentic capabilities.

Last week also saw a since-deleted Apple job listing detailing plans for autonomous AI agents.

We’ve already seen some of the ways in which this can go wrong, and we recently outlined three significant risks. Wired reports that banks are now responding to these by either blocking AI agents or warning customers that using them can be dangerous.

JPMorgan Chase changed its terms to ban third-party agents that log in with your credentials. That same day, Bank of America warned its customers not to share login info with agents. Along with the announced change coming from Wells Fargo, Citibank and PNC have also changed their terms to include warnings about agents.

Wells Fargo even goes as far as using capitals in its latest terms, stating that it will not be responsible for the consequences.

Your use of any AI Agent is AT YOUR OWN RISK

We can likely expect similar pushback in sectors like online shopping as companies fear high returns costs and other consequences from mistakes by AI agents.

Personally, I don’t give any AI agents access to any of my banking or other financial services, considering the risks to be too high. I don’t see my position changing any time soon.

What’s your take? Would you trust an AI agent with access to your bank accounts? If not, would Apple launching agentic capabilities for Siri AI change your view? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

#3258. Atomically Thin Materials Significantly Shrink Qubits

MIT researchers use 2D materials for capacitors in quantum circuits in an effort to scale processors

Superconducting quantum processor and its microwave packaging.

Quantum computing is a devilishly complex technology, with many technical hurdles impacting its development. Of these challenges two critical issues stand out: miniaturization and qubit quality.

IBM has adopted the superconducting qubit road map of reaching a 1,121-qubit processor by 2023, leading to the expectation that 1,000 qubits with today’s qubit form factor is feasible. However, current approaches will require very large chips (50 millimeters on a side, or larger) at the scale of small wafers, or the use of chiplets on multichip modules. While this approach will work, the aim is to attain a better path toward scalability.

Now researchers at MIT have been able to both reduce the size of the qubits and done so in a way that reduces the interference that occurs between neighboring qubits. The MIT researchers have increased the number of superconducting qubits that can be added onto a device by a factor of 100.

“We are addressing both qubit miniaturization and quality,” said William Oliver, the director for the Center for Quantum Engineering at MIT. “Unlike conventional transistor scaling, where only the number really matters, for qubits, large numbers are not sufficient, they must also be high-performance. Sacrificing performance for qubit number is not a useful trade in quantum computing. They must go hand in hand.”

The key to this big increase in qubit density and reduction of interference comes down to the use of two-dimensional materials, in particular the 2D insulator hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). The MIT researchers demonstrated that a few atomic monolayers of hBN can be stacked to form the insulator in the capacitors of a superconducting qubit.

Just like other capacitors, the capacitors in these superconducting circuits take the form of a sandwich in which an insulator material is sandwiched between two metal plates. The big difference for these capacitors is that the superconducting circuits can operate only at extremely low temperatures—less than 0.02 degrees above absolute zero (-273.15 °C).

Superconducting qubits are measured at temperatures as low as 20 millikelvin in a dilution refrigerator.Nathan Fiske/MIT

In that environment, insulating materials that are available for the job, such as PE-CVD silicon oxide or silicon nitride, have quite a few defects that are too lossy for quantum computing applications. To get around these material shortcomings, most superconducting circuits use what are called coplanar capacitors. In these capacitors, the plates are positioned laterally to one another, rather than on top of one another.

As a result, the intrinsic silicon substrate below the plates and to a smaller degree the vacuum above the plates serve as the capacitor dielectric. Intrinsic silicon is chemically pure and therefore has few defects, and the large size dilutes the electric field at the plate interfaces, all of which leads to a low-loss capacitor. The lateral size of each plate in this open-face design ends up being quite large (typically 100 by 100 micrometers) in order to achieve the required capacitance.

In an effort to move away from the large lateral configuration, the MIT researchers embarked on a search for an insulator that has very few defects and is compatible with superconducting capacitor plates.

“We chose to study hBN because it is the most widely used insulator in 2D material research due to its cleanliness and chemical inertness,” said colead author Joel Wang, a research scientist in the Engineering Quantum Systems group of the MIT Research Laboratory for Electronics.

On either side of the hBN, the MIT researchers used the 2D superconducting material, niobium diselenide. One of the trickiest aspects of fabricating the capacitors was working with the niobium diselenide, which oxidizes in seconds when exposed to air, according to Wang. This necessitates that the assembly of the capacitor occur in a glove box filled with argon gas.

While this would seemingly complicate the scaling up of the production of these capacitors, Wang doesn’t regard this as a limiting factor.

“What determines the quality factor of the capacitor are the two interfaces between the two materials,” said Wang. “Once the sandwich is made, the two interfaces are “sealed” and we don’t see any noticeable degradation over time when exposed to the atmosphere.”

This lack of degradation is because around 90 percent of the electric field is contained within the sandwich structure, so the oxidation of the outer surface of the niobium diselenide does not play a significant role anymore. This ultimately makes the capacitor footprint much smaller, and it accounts for the reduction in cross talk between the neighboring qubits.

“The main challenge for scaling up the fabrication will be the wafer-scale growth of hBN and 2D superconductors like [niobium diselenide], and how one can do wafer-scale stacking of these films,” added Wang.

Wang believes that this research has shown 2D hBN to be a good insulator candidate for superconducting qubits. He says that the groundwork the MIT team has done will serve as a road map for using other hybrid 2D materials to build superconducting circuits.

Dexter Johnson is a contributing editor at IEEE Spectrum, with a focus on nanotechnology.

#3257. Nintendo's Black Friday Deals Are Actually Pretty Good

Black Friday is nearly upon us. From now through Cyber Monday, retailers and companies alike are offering deals and discounts on their wares. While I always keep an eye out for Nintendo deals offered by stores like Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart, it seems the company is offering its own discounts this year—and, surprisingly, they're actually pretty solid.

Last Thursday, Nintendo announced its Black Friday discounts. We've already seen Switch 2 sales ahead of the Black Friday season, but now, Nintendo has confirmed an official discount for the console.

Starting Nov. 22 through Dec. 5, you can pick up Nintendo's Switch 2 Mario Kart bundle for $499.00, down $50 from $549.99. That includes the console, a download of Mario Kart World, and a 90-day Nintendo Switch Online Individual Membership.

If you already have a Switch 2 console and/or Mario Kart World, you're not left out of the Black Friday deals here. From Nov. 22 through Nov. 29, Nintendo is also running discounts on several high-profile Switch and Switch 2 games:

Donkey Kong Bananza was one of Nintendo's launch titles for the Switch 2. And while it's been out for over a year, Donkey Kong's first 3D game is still among the best-reviewed titles on the console. Nintendo is taking $20 off the game's MSRP for this promotion.

Kirby Air Riders on Switch 2 is only the second installment in the series. The original launched all the way back on the GameCube, and while the title typically runs for $69.99, Nintendo is letting it go for $49.99.

Metroid Prime 4 arrived last year after an 18-year wait from Metroid Prime 3: Corruption. The game typically retails for $69.99 for a physical copy on Switch 2, but Nintendo is selling it for $49 during its early Black Friday promotion.

Super Mario Galaxy (both the original and the sequel) are beloved by fans. These titles originally launched on the Wii, and Nintendo rereleased both for the Switch. (The company offers a free upgrade to the Switch 2 edition.) Nintendo asks $69.99 for this combo, and while you can find it for under $60, you'll officially be able to pick it up for $48.97 before Black Friday.

Nintendo's latest Mario Party, Jamboree, has a Switch 2 edition with a rather staggering MSRP of $79.99. While it's the version of the game with the most features, it's also the most expensive. You'll be able to buy it for $39.99 for Black Friday, saving up to $40.

Nintendo rarely offers official discounts on some of its biggest titles, especially in this current era. In addition, Nintendo announced a sale on its digital store that runs from Nov. 19 through Dec. 2, though it didn't say which titles would be on sale. Just keep an eye on all these dates: The Switch 2 console promotion runs longer than the physical and digital games discounts, while the digital sale runs longer than the physical sale. Nintendo says that these discounts will be available "at select retailers," as well as its brick-and-mortar locations in New York and San Francisco. You can also buy the Switch 2 bundle through Nintendo's website.

It depends! Its Nintendo Switch 2 bundle deal runs from Nov. 22 through Dec. 5; the select games listed above will be on sale from Nov. 22 through Nov. 29; and digital titles will have discounts from Nov. 19 through Dec. 2.

While we don't know which digital titles will be discounted yet, we do know that physical copies of Donkey Kong Bananza, Kirby Air Riders, Metroid Prime 4: Beyond, Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2, and Super Mario Party: Jamboree will be on sale for $39.99 each.

Yes! The Switch 2 alone costs $499.99, so you essentially get the game for free. Mario Kart World is also one of the console's best multiplayer titles right now, so it makes sense to pick it up in this bundle.

#3256. Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO of Nvidia, stock up 30%

Nvidia has announced that disgraced CEO Jensen Huang has been reinstated to the role, effective immediately. The company’s share price jumped more than 30% in response, with the rest of the market also making significant gains.

It said that the board voted unanimously in favor of reinstatement despite its recent statement that it had no intention of doing so …

Huang’s affair with a woman suspected to be a Chinese spy became the main headline news in the tech press after coming to light at the end of last month. The New York Times broke the story on October 29, citing it then as “a close relationship.” Nvidia initially denied that the relationship was anything out of the ordinary.

That changed on November 8 when Huang publicly admitted to the affair. Nvidia’s shares dropped 5%, and the company’s board of directors opened an independent investigation. Further details emerged over the following days. Things got even worse when the same paper reported that Huang had also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him.

That led to Huang being fired resigning on November 12.

Money over country. This is government intervention.

Despite putting the company at enormous risk and initially lying to its board of directors, there were calls in some quarters for Huang to be reinstated. He responded by saying that he would be “honored” to return if asked to do so.

The board of directors, however, said that it had no intention of inviting him back.

Nvidia’s chair Harvey Jones said: “The board does not intend to reinstate him.”

That changed today, with the company making the announcement in a press release.

Nvidia today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board. The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.” Harvey Jones will remain as Board chair.

“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”

As previously announced, in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, the Board formed a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate, and the committee retained independent counsel to assist it in that investigation. The Board reiterated that the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion. Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it.

The company’s stock price jumped by more than 30% in response, with the rest of the market also up per Yahoo Finance.

Nvidia shares soared more than 30% Monday morning […] The S&P 500 (^GSPC) rose 4.5% following seven straight days of declines. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) jumped more than 1,200 points to recover by 2.5% following its worst week since the COVID-related sell-off in 2020. The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) rallied 7%.

#3255. How AI Will Change Chip Design

Artificial intelligence’s promise and potential for the semiconductor industry

Rina Diane Caballar is a contributing editor covering tech and its intersections with science, society, and the environment.

An array of semiconductor wafers are ready to be made into chips.

The end of Moore’s Law is looming. Engineers and designers can do only so much to miniaturize transistors and pack as many of them as possible into chips. So they’re turning to other approaches to chip design, incorporating technologies like AI into the process.

Samsung, for instance, is adding AI to its memory chips to enable processing in memory, thereby saving energy and speeding up machine learning. Speaking of speed, Google’s TPU V4 AI chip has doubled its processing power compared with that of its previous version.

But AI holds still more promise and potential for the semiconductor industry. To better understand how AI is set to revolutionize chip design, we spoke with Heather Gorr, senior product manager for MathWorks’ MATLAB platform.

How is AI currently being used to design the next generation of chips?

Heather Gorr: AI is such an important technology because it’s involved in most parts of the cycle, including the design and manufacturing process. There’s a lot of important applications here, even in the general process engineering where we want to optimize things. I think defect detection is a big one at all phases of the process, especially in manufacturing. But even thinking ahead in the design process, [AI now plays a significant role] when you’re designing the light and the sensors and all the different components. There’s a lot of anomaly detection and fault mitigation that you really want to consider.

Then, thinking about the logistical modeling that you see in any industry, there is always planned downtime that you want to mitigate; but you also end up having unplanned downtime. So, looking back at that historical data of when you’ve had those moments where maybe it took a bit longer than expected to manufacture something, you can take a look at all of that data and use AI to try to identify the proximate cause or to see something that might jump out even in the processing and design phases. We think of AI oftentimes as a predictive tool, or as a robot doing something, but a lot of times you get a lot of insight from the data through AI.

What are the benefits of using AI for chip design?

Gorr: Historically, we’ve seen a lot of physics-based modeling, which is a very intensive process. We want to do a reduced order model, where instead of solving such a computationally expensive and extensive model, we can do something a little cheaper. You could create a surrogate model, so to speak, of that physics-based model, use the data, and then do your parameter sweeps, your optimizations, your Monte Carlo simulations using the surrogate model. That takes a lot less time computationally than solving the physics-based equations directly. So, we’re seeing that benefit in many ways, including the efficiency and economy that are the results of iterating quickly on the experiments and the simulations that will really help in the design.

So it’s like having a digital twin in a sense?

Gorr: Exactly. That’s pretty much what people are doing, where you have the physical system model and the experimental data. Then, in conjunction, you have this other model that you could tweak and tune and try different parameters and experiments that let sweep through all of those different situations and come up with a better design in the end.

So, it’s going to be more efficient and, as you said, cheaper?

Gorr: Yeah, definitely. Especially in the experimentation and design phases, where you’re trying different things. That’s obviously going to yield dramatic cost savings if you’re actually manufacturing and producing [the chips]. You want to simulate, test, experiment as much as possible without making something using the actual process engineering.

We’ve talked about the benefits. How about the drawbacks?

Gorr: The [AI-based experimental models] tend to not be as accurate as physics-based models. Of course, that’s why you do many simulations and parameter sweeps. But that’s also the benefit of having that digital twin, where you can keep that in mind—it’s not going to be as accurate as that precise model that we’ve developed over the years.

Both chip design and manufacturing are system intensive; you have to consider every little part. And that can be really challenging. It’s a case where you might have models to predict something and different parts of it, but you still need to bring it all together.

One of the other things to think about too is that you need the data to build the models. You have to incorporate data from all sorts of different sensors and different sorts of teams, and so that heightens the challenge.

How can engineers use AI to better prepare and extract insights from hardware or sensor data?

Gorr: We always think about using AI to predict something or do some robot task, but you can use AI to come up with patterns and pick out things you might not have noticed before on your own. People will use AI when they have high-frequency data coming from many different sensors, and a lot of times it’s useful to explore the frequency domain and things like data synchronization or resampling. Those can be really challenging if you’re not sure where to start.

One of the things I would say is, use the tools that are available. There’s a vast community of people working on these things, and you can find lots of examples [of applications and techniques] on GitHub or MATLAB Central, where people have shared nice examples, even little apps they’ve created. I think many of us are buried in data and just not sure what to do with it, so definitely take advantage of what’s already out there in the community. You can explore and see what makes sense to you, and bring in that balance of domain knowledge and the insight you get from the tools and AI.

What should engineers and designers consider when using AI for chip design?

Gorr: Think through what problems you’re trying to solve or what insights you might hope to find, and try to be clear about that. Consider all of the different components, and document and test each of those different parts. Consider all of the people involved, and explain and hand off in a way that is sensible for the whole team.

How do you think AI will affect chip designers’ jobs?

Gorr: It’s going to free up a lot of human capital for more advanced tasks. We can use AI to reduce waste, to optimize the materials, to optimize the design, but then you still have that human involved whenever it comes to decision-making. I think it’s a great example of people and technology working hand in hand. It’s also an industry where all people involved—even on the manufacturing floor—need to have some level of understanding of what’s happening, so this is a great industry for advancing AI because of how we test things and how we think about them before we put them on the chip.

How do you envision the future of AI and chip design?

Gorr: It’s very much dependent on that human element—involving people in the process and having that interpretable model. We can do many things with the mathematical minutiae of modeling, but it comes down to how people are using it, how everybody in the process is understanding and applying it. Communication and involvement of people of all skill levels in the process are going to be really important. We’re going to see less of those superprecise predictions and more transparency of information, sharing, and that digital twin—not only using AI but also using our human knowledge and all of the work that many people have done over the years.

Rina Diane Caballar is a writer covering tech and its intersections with science, society, and the environment. An IEEE Spectrum contributing editor, she's a former software engineer based in New Zealand.

#3254. 20 of the Coolest Tech Stocking Stuffers for Under $50

This series will help you pick the perfect presents, decor, and activities to make this Christmas the Best Christmas Ever.

What if you make this the year you don't fill all the stockings with candy or gift cards? Both have their place, but if you want to make this the best Christmas ever, you have to shove some tech in those stockings. The good news: Tech gifts don’t have to be expensive to be impressive.

No matter who you're shopping for, there are tons of affordable gizmos that are some combination of cool and useful and that feel pricier than they are. Here are 20 cool tech stocking stuffers to light up any holiday morning, all of which cost less than $50.

If there's an old-school gamer on your list, their Christmas morning will be extra merry if it includes a tiny video game emulator. R36T Retro Gaming Console ($48.98) puts over 18,000 video games in the palm of your hand. It has a 3.5" screen, so whether they like arcade classics or consoles-of-the-past, they can fit 'em all in a pocket.

The Xteink X4 is an e-reader that's smaller than your phone. It uses e-ink like an Amazon Kindle, so you can whip a glare-free screen out of your pocket and start reading anywhere there's a light source. The X4 is a no-frills gadget—there's no lighting, touchscreen, or apps—but if you want a cheap, convenient way to read for around $50, it's perfect.

Those disposable cans of compressed air with the red straws are so 2015. Blow the dust off your electronics with an SDFM Electric Air Duster instead. With an engine that moves at 150,000 RPM, it shoots air such high speeds, the dust doesn't stand a chance. It's also cordless and comes with a variety of cleaning attachments to keep your gear in top shape.

If your giftee likes to listen to music or podcasts while drifting off to sleep, the only gift better than a pair of sleep headphones is two pairs of sleep headphones! This two-pack retails for $22.99 and contains two headbands with built in speakers you can pair with your phone or other device easily.

Your giftee may have the tech side of their battle station/home office locked down, but I bet they don't have the aesthetics dialed in. Govee Smart LED Light Bars ($54.99, but currently on sale for $34.99) are programmable, colorful light bars that work with Alexa and Google Assistant and can display light effects created from 16 millions colors. It even syncs with your music to provide trippy visuals.

My lifestyle doesn't involve cutting down trees, but I still need one of these miniature chainsaws. I mean, it's a chainsaw, and it's only six inches long. This Seeii mini chainsaw ($49.99) is battery-powered, so no one will be accidentally cutting the cord. According to the listing, it's suitable for tree pruning, garden artistry, shrub trimming, forest logging, and wood cutting.

You know what computer fiends are missing in their lives? Knobs. This little $33 gadget lets you assign functions to four external knobs and 12 push buttons, so you can finally have a decent volume control, scrub through video smoothly, skip music tracks with a button push, and control any other function easily and physically. Perfect for gamers.

You could use a tape measure like a caveman, or you could measure things with a frickin' laser that fits in your pocket. This $40 gadget has an LED screen that's easy to read and it doubles as a cat toy. But does it measure things? Damn right it measures things—big things, little things, middle-sized things—it doesn't care what you put in front of it, it will measure the hell out of it! (Up to 98 feet, anyway.)

This compact Bluetooth speaker has an Amazon rating of 4.6 stars out of 5, and it's cheap—just $45. It's waterproof, it sounds great, and it features a built-in light show with six different settings so you can check out cool visuals with your tunes.

A single Apple Airtag makes a great gift to accompany the main gift you don't want someone to lose. Or they can put it on their wallet or your keys, and if they misplace them, they can hit a button and it will play a sound while the FindMy app displays a map that leads to the missing item. Plus, it works in reverse, so you can hit a tag and it will ring your lost phone.

If you want to give the gift of warmth for the holidays, you could do a lot worse than this portable neck, shoulder, and back warmer. There are three temperature settings, a safety shut-off feature, and it heats up really fast, for only $33.

This tiny little vacuum from Odistar will keep their desktop dust-free. It sucks with 1000Pa of suction power for 400 minutes off a single charge, and it's very easy to use: You put it in the palm of your hand and push it around. Cool!

It's not like people need an endoscope camera every day, but if the need for a tiny camera does arise—if they need to see why the engine isn't working or if their wedding ring falls behind the oven—they'll be glad to have this Anykit USB Endoscope Camera. It plugs right into an Android or iPhone and captures HD photos and video of places the sun don't shine.

If your giftee is carrying their laptop around to coffeehouses like a chump, this is the perfect present. They can connect a foldable mini Bluetooth keyboard from iClever to their phone, and turn it into an ultra-portable productivity device. It even has a little trackpad!

This skinny extra battery charges a phone magnetically or with a USB-C cable. It's fast, too. It can charge an iPhone 16 Pro Max to 37% in 30 minutes via the USB-C port and it's less than three inches wide.

Projectors have gotten really good and really small over the last few years, and they prices have come down massively too. This mini projector costs only $29 and projects a 720p image up to 120" and it weighs only about two pounds.

Most people already have a media streamer attached to their televisions, but in case you're gifting someone who doesn't, the Roku Streaming Stick 4K is a solid choice in the $50 price range. This no-frills device serves up 4K HD video, gives you access to hundreds of free and premium channels, and is easy to setup.

The Twelve South AirFly SE is an ultra-compact Bluetooth transmitter lets you plug into any device with a 3.5 mm jack, like in-flight entertainment systems, gym machines, or TVs, and stream audio wirelessly to your Bluetooth earbuds or headphones. Leave those accursed wired headphone in the drawer where they belong!

This is an essential gift if there's a cyclist in your life and anyone who wants to maintain proper PSI in their car tires. This portable air compressor weighs less than a pound and is a steal at only $40. It's rechargeable, has an onboard pressure gauge, an LED flashlight, and can inflate a car tire in only eight minutes.

I am 100% sure anyone you give this to will be able to use it. This compact, high‑power Anker charger has two USB‑C ports plus one USB‑A, letting you power up your laptop, phone, and tablet all at once, from one plug. Plus it charges fast.

Black Friday streaming deals are your chance to score massive discounts on the best streaming services. Popular platforms are up to 75% off, and with price hikes all too common, these discounts are even more valuable.

My favorite discount today (November 25) is the Disney+/Hulu bundle for $4.99 a month; two streaming services for one low monthly price. Or how about HBO Max for $5.49 a month for a full year, or the overlooked Apple TV for $6.99 a month. These are just the start of the seasonal offers.

Below, I'm rounding up all the biggest Black Friday streaming deals to help you reduce your monthly entertainment bill without losing access to a favorite streaming library. Plus, I'm highlighting new deals as they go live.

Even at full price, the Disney+ and Hulu bundle is a great deal, but for Black Friday it's an even bigger bargain at $4.99 per month. The two services pair together perfectly, with Disney+'s library ideal for families, and Hulu giving grown-ups plenty to watch. Even better, this discounted price is available for 12 months, an offer few rivals can match. Right now, this is the Black Friday streaming deal to beat.

Paramount+ has discounted every tier to $2.99, so the choice is obvious: get Paramount+ Premium. With this top-tier package, you get full access to the Paramount+ library with ad-free streaming, Showtime originals, and your local CBS station. There's plenty to watch, from the final season of "Yellowjackets" to live sports, like NFL and Champions League soccer. The only downside is that this offer is only valid for 2 months, which feels stingy compared to rivals.

Apple TV is a streaming service you shouldn't overlook. It packs one of the best original libraries of any streamer, with a wealth of must-watch TV shows you can't find anywhere else. Ahead of Black Friday, Apple TV is 50% off, giving you six months of access for $6.99 a month. That's enough time to binge a wide selection of the very best Apple TV Originals from "Severance" to "Slow Horses".

HBO Max is our top-rated streaming service and is also 50% off in this epic Black Friday deal. You won't find a platform with a better library, because after all, it's not just TV; it's HBO! This discount is available for a full year, and if you sign up now, you'll be all set ahead of the debut of HBO's new "Harry Potter" show in December.

After sitting on the sidelines last year, Peacock returns with a Black Friday deal for 2026. The cheapest Select tier is just $2.99, but I most recommend the Premium tier, as you get full access to Peacock's library of shows, movies, live sports, originals, and more. At $8.99, this isn't the most headline-grabbing Black Friday deal right now, but it's a decent saving on a solid streamer.

Prime Video add-on subscriptions: deals from $0.99Prime Video add-on subscriptions add entire new libraries to Amazon's streaming service, giving you plenty to watch. Deals start from $0.99 and include Paramount+, HBO Max, Apple TV, MGM+, Hallmark+, Starz, Crunchyroll, AMC+, BritBox and more. Whatever you like to watch, you'll almost certainly find a Prime Video subscription that appeals to your tastes.

Good morning! Black Friday is getting ever closer, but you don't need to wait until the day itself to start saving on the best streaming services because the holiday deals have already arrived, and in this live blog the Tom's Guide streaming team will be highlighting all the biggest savings on the streaming services worth your money.

The deal that's caught my eye the most this week is the Disney+ and Hulu bundle for $4.99 per month, for 12 months (yup, a full year of discounted streaming). This bundle typically costs $11.99, and I've recommended it at that price quite a few times in the past, so now at more than 50% off, it's a deal that you really should consider.

For Black Friday, Prime Video has discounted a whole bunch of its add-on subscriptions, if you're unaware of these, they let you access whole streaming services within the Prime Video UI. There's big hitters like Paramount+, Peacock and Apple TV, alongside more overlooked, but still worthwhile, services like MGM+, AMC+ and Starz. Check out the full selection of Prime Video add-ons on sale down below!

Paramount+ is doing Black Friday a little differently compared to some of its streaming rivals. Every tier is on sale for $2.99, which means there's really no reason not to opt for the Premium package. However, this discounted rate is only available for two months, which is disappointing compared to the 6-12 months offered by other platforms. Still, for just shy of $6, you can enjoy Paramount+ through the whole holiday season, so this is still a Black Friday streaming deal to grab now.

HBO Max ranks as our favorite streaming service here at Tom's Guide, and thanks to this Black Friday deal, you can sign up for $5.49 per month for 12 months; that's a full year at 50% off. Now's a great time to get HBO Max in your streaming setup because not only do you have a stacked library to enjoy right now, but a little show called "Harry Potter" is on its way and will debut on Christmas Day (Dec. 25).

If price is your primary concern, and you want access to a whole new library at the lowest cost possible, then check out this deal: Frndly TV is $0.99 per month, down from $12.99. The platform gives you access to a bunch of live TV channels: Hallmark, A&E, History, Lifetime, The Weather Channel, and a whole lot more. Plus, there's an "On Demand" library, if you want to catch up without tuning in live!

Apple TV doesn't always get the credit it deserves, but with this Black Friday deal, now is a great time to discover why it's originals library is so highly rated. Okay, so its movie offering is a little on the slimmer side, but when it comes to high-quality TV you won't find anywhere else, Apple TV competes with the very best. You can get six months of Apple TV for $6.99 per month ahead of Black Friday.

It's not just the best streaming services on sale for Black Friday, streaming sticks are also discounted, and after all there's no point saving on streaming platforms without a suitable way to watch movies/shows on your television. Amazon has discounted (almost) the entire range of Fire TV Sticks with deals starting from just $15 right now.

A little movie called "Avengers: Doomsday" is hitting theaters in less than a month, so I'm using the next few weeks to refresh my memory of my favorite Marvel movies (and also catch up on some of the TV shows I skipped). Disney+ is the streaming home of the MCU, so it's well-timed that you can get access to the complete MCU for just $4.99 per month thanks to the excellent Disney+ and Hulu bundle deal.

If, like me, you've recently watched "You Can See Everything," and are looking for more Nathan Fielder, then I recommend "The Curse" on Paramount+, a zany cringe-comedy that stars Fielder and Emma Stone. It sees a newly-wed couple trying to bring eco-living to a small New Mexico town, and getting entangled with a TV producer (Benny Safdie) and a mysterious curse, and things very quickly go south from there. Grab Paramount+ for $2.99 and check out this oddball, acclaimed show.

If you want Peacock at it's lowest price, then the Select tier is discounted to $2.99. But if you want my advice, this isn't a great package, because the limitations are pretty huge. It excludes movies, sports and Peacock Originals, only giving you access to TV shows from NBC, Bravo and other networks. If you really want Peacock at a low price, it might be worth considering, but I'd strongly recommend picking Premium.

The latest "Hunger Games" movie, "Sunrise on the Reaping," just hit theaters, and if you're looking to catch up on the franchise before heading to your local multiplex, the whole franchise is streaming on Hulu (which is $4.99 paired with Disney+ for Black Friday), which includes the original quartet led by Jennifer Lawrence and the first prequel flick, "The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes." Get streaming now!

The holiday season is in the air, and that means Hallmark movies! The network is known for its massive slate of new Christmas movies each year, and in 2026 that includes a seasonal flick starring Lacey Chabert, and set at Disney World! Thanks to this Prime Video add-on subscription deal, you can get access to Hallmark+ for $2.25/month (saving almost 75%). The deal runs for 3 months, which is more than enough to get you through the holiday season and watch dozens of festive films!

Even as somebody who covers streaming daily, I hadn't heard of Howdy until this week, but the platform is currently $0.99 a month for two months via Prime Video. That's a very cheap deal, for a service with a surprisingly strong movie library.

You can watch "One Battle After Another," "Weapons," "Knives Out," and plenty more worthwhile flicks. Oh and also the HBO anthology series "Love Life," which I have a soft spot for, and the Emmy-nominated "Hemlock Grove". Howdy doesn't look to have the most robust library, but for a buck a month, you'll get your monies worth.

If you love dark TV shows, then MGM+ (on sale for $1.99 per month via Prime Video) is home to some of the best around right now, namely "From" and "The Institute." Both shows are dark and twisted, and will have you hooked from the first episode. MGM+ also has plenty to offer non-horror fans like "Project Hail Mary," the feel-good sci-fi blockbuster that sees Ryan Gosling team up with an extraterrestrial.

Hey, it's Alix here, a senior streaming writer on the team, taking over the live blog! As someone who spends pretty much every day keeping up with the latest streaming releases, deals and subscription changes, I've got my eye on all the best Black Friday offers.The first deal I have to mention is HBO Max, if only for the chance to watch the incredible "IT: Welcome to Derry" if you haven't already. It's one of my favorite shows of 2025, so I'm always going to recommend giving it a watch! But there's another big reason to consider signing up: HBO Max will also be home to the upcoming "Harry Potter" series, which is set to make its debut this Christmas.

That's a pretty good incentive to lock in a cheaper subscription now, especially if you're planning on sticking around for the wizarding world to return to our screens. At only $5.49 a month for 12 months, you can't go wrong.

Starz is one I'd urge you not to overlook, especially when it's just $2.99 as an add-on through Prime Video. It's home to some brilliant shows, including "Sweetpea," starring Ella Purnell, which has a second season on the way, plus "Outlander: Blood of My Blood" and "Power: Legacy," with more to look forward to in the new year. There's also a pretty impressive library of movies to work your way through, making this a surprisingly good little add-on for the price.

Anime fans should also take a look at Crunchyroll, which has dropped its Fan plan to just $3.99 a month for the first six months, down from $9.99. That's a pretty hefty saving for access to its extensive anime library, completely ad-free streaming, offline viewing and new episodes shortly after they air in Japan.

It's a great opportunity to dive into some new series or catch up on your watchlist without spending a fortune. Just remember that the price returns to the standard monthly rate after six months!

Unfortunately, I wouldn't hold your breath. Netflix has never really been one to join the Black Friday festivities, and 2026 looks set to be no different. So, sadly, there's no surprise Christmas gift or cheaper subscription coming from the streaming giant this year.

But that doesn't mean there aren't plenty of other fantastic deals worth checking out! It's also a great opportunity to take stock of your subscriptions, cancel any services you're barely using and perhaps try something new while it's available at a much lower price. Your wallet will thank you!

One deal I really wouldn't sleep on is the Disney+ and Hulu bundle, which is down to just $4.99 a month for 12 months, compared to its usual $12.99 monthly price. That's both services for less than $60 for an entire year!

Between Disney's Marvel, Star Wars and Pixar library and Hulu's brilliant originals, dramas and reality TV, there's a ridiculous amount of content to get through. It's easily one of the best streaming bargains this Black Friday, so I'd definitely get in before the offer disappears at the end of November 30.

If there's one Black Friday deal I'd recommend horror fans and TV lovers jump on, it's AMC+. You can get the Premium ad-free plan for just $2.75 a month for two months, down from $10.99, through Prime Video. There's also an ad-supported option for just $1.99, but I'd personally spend the extra 76 cents to skip the commercials.

And where would I start with the library? Well, naturally, my first pick would be "The Walking Dead" universe. You've got the main series, "Fear the Walking Dead," "Daryl Dixon," "Dead City" and "The Ones Who Live," so there's plenty to keep you occupied. You'll also find brilliant shows like "Mad Men," "Breaking Bad," "Better Call Saul" and "Interview with the Vampire." Honestly, that's a lot of entertainment for less than the price of a coffee!

It's not just streaming services that have discounts. You can take advantage of Black Friday to make your streaming setup a little better without spending a fortune. The Roku Streaming Stick HD is a great little upgrade, particularly if you've got an older TV that doesn't have all the apps you need.

It plugs straight into your TV, giving you access to popular streaming services, hundreds of free live TV channels and a voice remote that also controls your TV's power and volume. It's currently $19 down from $39 at Amazon, making it a handy Black Friday pick for anyone looking to get more out of their TV without buying a new one.

One tip before you go signing up for everything: don't forget to cancel your subscriptions once the discounted periods come to an end, particularly if you don't plan on keeping them. Many of these deals automatically renew at the regular monthly price, which can quickly eat into the money you've saved.

I'd recommend setting a reminder on your phone for a few days before each deal expires. That way, you can enjoy all the extra streaming without any surprises on your bank statement!

Sports fans, don't overlook Fox One! You can currently grab a subscription through Prime Video for just $4.99 for your first month, down from the usual $19.99. That's a whopping 75% saving and gets you access to live sports across FOX, FS1, FS2, Big Ten Network and more, including NFL, MLB and college football coverage.

Just remember that it'll automatically jump back to the regular monthly price after your first month, so cancel if you don't plan on keeping it.

Peacock is another one I'd definitely add to your Black Friday subscriptions, especially if you've been meaning to catch up on its growing collection of originals. I'd personally go for Premium, as it unlocks the full library of movies, Peacock Originals and live sports, including NFL and Premier League coverage.

You've also got "The Traitors," "The Office," "Yellowstone" and plenty of Bravo favorites to keep you busy. Both offers are available until November 30, so don't leave it too late!

Don't sleep on Paramount+, because I'd argue it has one of the strongest lineups of original TV shows around. From "Yellowjackets" and "Dexter: Resurrection" to "Tulsa King," "Lioness," "MobLand" and "South Park," there's a lot more here than you might initially think.

Even better, you can get Paramount+ Premium for just $2.99 a month for your first two months, down from $13.99. That's the top-tier, ad-free on-demand plan. It features a built-in subwoofer, 3.1-channel audio, Dolby Atmos and DTS:X support, plus dedicated dialogue channels to help bring a little more clarity to your favorite shows and movies. It's a particularly tempting upgrade if your TV's built-in speakers aren't doing your favorite blockbusters justice.

Through its add-on subscriptions, you can sign up for the likes of HBO Max, Starz, AMC+, Apple TV, Peacock and plenty more, all accessible through the same Prime Video app and billed through your Amazon account.

It’s particularly handy if you’re jumping between services to take advantage of Black Friday deals, as you don’t need to keep downloading different apps or juggling multiple logins. You can also manage and cancel your subscriptions in just a few clicks. It’s a pretty convenient way to keep all your streaming under one roof!

Apple TV is another Black Friday deal I wouldn't pass up, particularly if you're a fan of quality originals. You can currently get six months for just $6.99 a month, down from the usual $14.99, saving you more than 50%.

And there's plenty to keep you entertained, including the brilliant "Severance," "Slow Horses," "Silo," "Shrinking," "Ted Lasso" and "Pluribus." There's also a growing selection of movies, including "F1," "The Gorge" and "Wolfs." Best of all, Apple TV is completely ad-free, so you can enjoy all those fantastic shows without interruptions.

I jumped into the streaming deals to take over for Alix and was immediately attracted to that Disney+ and Hulu deal for $4.99 a month for 12 months, so I logged into my lapsed Disney+ account and signed up.

You really can't go wrong with two well-regarded streaming services for only $4.99. If you're on the fence about what streaming deals to grab, I highly advise you to go with that one, especially if you have young people in the home who will enjoy the massive library of Disney movies (plus you get Marvel, Star Wars and all the films and shows).

If you're thinking about cutting down your streaming bill without sacrificing your entertainment, you'll want to follow her lead! You'll need to jump through a few hoops, but it's worth it what could amount to a whole year of savings.

After all, Halloween 2027 is basically just around the corner, and you'll want to make sure you're prepared.

Amazon's Prime Video has a whole bunch of its add-on subscriptions discounted.

Amazon offers some serious big names like Paramount+, Peacock and Apple TV+. It even has some of the more overlooked services like MGM+, AMC+ and Starz. It's definitely worth getting into the Prime Video add-ons below and seeing where you can snag some savings.

Now that season 2 of Stick has hit the streaming service, and with the Black Friday deal getting you Apple TV for $6.99 per month, it's the perfect time to binge both seasons.

When streaming services run Black Friday deals, as they are now, the prices we see first are usually for the ad-supported versions.

But do you prefer to pay the extra for ad-free viewing, or are you content to sit through a few minutes of ads to save some money?

Most of you probably already have a TV to watch these awesome streaming deals on.

But if, for some reason, you don't, or you're looking to upgrade your current TV to something a little nicer, the Roku 65-inch Pro OLED TV is an absolutely absurd deal at $799. Once you experience your favorite content on an OLED TV, you'll never want to watch stuff any other way.

If you're a Plex user and you haven't taken the plunge on a Plex Pass yet, there's no better time than Black Friday, as it's currently 40% off whether you go monthly, yearly, 5 years or lifetime.

That puts the monthly cost down to $4.19, the yearly down to $41.99, 5 years down to $149.99 and lifetime down to $449.99. Whichever length you choose, 40% off is a sizable discount.

In case you haven't been paying attention, HBO Max is 50% off for Black Friday. That's $5..49 per month for some of the best shows and movies you can get on any streaming service.

Just don't get too attached to any characters when watching HBO Originals. We all know how that typically ends...

If your idea of holiday cheer involves a little Austen-era drama, BritBox is about to make your Black Friday shopping a lot more interesting. The streaming service is dropping to just $2.75/month (down from $10.99) through Prime Video Channels, making it a steal for anyone itching to watch "The Other Bennet Sister" and its upcoming Christmas special. The three-part installment continues to follow Mary Bennet's story.

And if that's not enough period-drama goodness to justify the subscription, BritBox has plenty more British mysteries, swoon-worthy romances and gripping dramas to keep you occupied long after the holiday leftovers are gone.
